title: Ревность Дениса и бега тараканов  (Denis's Jealousy and Cockroach Races)

segments.t: At Boutique Hotel Eleon the day before the grand opening, Katya confronts Denis over his constant jealousy while Senya and Fedya stage cockroach races in the back room. Listen to the full exchange first.
Ей нравится, когда ей доверяет парень.
Он ведёт себя как ревнивый парень.
Я как будто в театр сходил.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
'I am listening to you.' The grammar packs 'to listen' and 'you' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'The grand opening is tomorrow.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'grand opening' before landing on 'tomorrow'. Denis answers right away.
'I have no idea.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'concept' before landing on 'to have'.
'Come on, that is all.' Denis anchors the line on 'come on', while 'everything' completes the thought.
'Hi, Denis.' The grammar packs 'hello' and 'Denis' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Denis answers right away.
'Did something happen?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'and' before landing on 'happened'.
'No, nothing.' In Russian, the idea of 'no' flows naturally into 'nothing' without extra filler words.
Ей нравится, когда ей доверяет парень.
'She likes it when her boyfriend trusts her.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'to her' and finishing on 'boyfriend'.
Он ведёт себя как ревнивый парень.
'He behaves like a jealous boyfriend.' Notice how Russian expresses 'he' and 'boyfriend' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'You two argue really coolly.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'you' before landing on 'you argue'.
Я как будто в театр сходил.
'It is as if I went to the theater.' Notice how Russian expresses 'I' and 'went' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'No more bets.' Senya anchors the line on 'of bets', while 'no' completes the thought.
'And start!' The meaning hinges on 'and' working together with 'begin' in spoken Russian.

'Today we have a draw.' Russians say 'by me' or 'with us' where English says 'I have' or 'we have', without needing a separate word for 'have'. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.
Ей нравится, когда ей доверяет парень.
Он ведёт себя как ревнивый парень.
Я как будто в театр сходил.
And that finishes our first look inside Boutique Hotel Eleon. Listen for the reflexive verb ending on the word for arguing. See you next time!
